key_insight: A single-stage Huffman encoder compresses data for distributed ML without the separate frequency analysis, codebook generation, and codebook transmission steps, cutting computational and latency overhead while preserving lossless compression benefits.
problem_solved: Eliminates the three-stage Huffman workflow that adds compute, latency, and extra data (codebook) overhead—bottlenecks for latency-sensitive distributed training and inference across accelerators and networks.
method: Integrate frequency estimation and code assignment into a single pass so encoding happens without a separate codebook generation stage.
Use a deterministic/shared encoding scheme (or on-the-fly derivation) to avoid sending a per-chunk codebook with the data.
Implement a low-overhead encoder optimized for accelerator/communication pipelines to minimize added CPU/GPU latency.
impact: Reduces network bandwidth and end-to-end latency for multi-accelerator ML workloads, enabling faster distributed training and lower-cost serving without sacrificing lossless compression.
visual_elements: Before vs After pipeline diagram: three-stage Huffman (freq analysis → codebook gen → transmit+compress) vs single-stage encoder (single-pass encode, no codebook transmit).
Bar chart showing reduced latency and network bytes for single-stage vs traditional Huffman across typical batch sizes.
Network diagram illustrating fewer packets/overhead between accelerators when using single-stage encoding.
Icon set: stopwatch (latency), cylinder/network (bandwidth), shield (lossless integrity), gear (low compute overhead).
paper_title: Single-Stage Huffman Encoder for ML Compression
paper_authors: Aditya Agrawal, Albert Magyar, Hiteshwar Eswaraiah, Patrick Sheridan, Pradeep Janedula
